tags.name: Cali Ship Wreck
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-pulled underanendlesssky.com, padi.com, tortugadivers.com. Length 220ft confirmed by 2 sources (Under An Endless Sky, PADI); the '206ft' figure could not be re-confirmed this pass. Sinking date conflict found: majority of sources (Under An Endless Sky, Red Sail, Tortuga) say 9 Jan 1948 (leak at sea, run aground, burned, then dynamited); PADI's site page instead states 1944 due to 'severe weather' — flagged as a source conflict in the description rather than silently picking one. Depth 6-9m (20-30ft) reconfirmed by Red Sail and Tortuga. No changes to marine life claims (tarpon/angelfish already site-confirmed).

tags.name: USS Kittiwake Shipwreck
tags.qa_notes: RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23 — HALLUCINATION CORRECTED: The previous QA pass's claim that the Kittiwake 'recovered the Challenger's flight data recorder' is ITSELF FALSE and has been removed. Re-verified directly against en.wikipedia.org and divetech.com ('What did the Kittiwake do?'): the Space Shuttle Challenger was not equipped with a flight data recorder/black box at all — the Kittiwake recovered a large curved debris segment from the right Solid Rocket Booster (SRB) on 17 April 1986 from ~175 fsw. Description and qa_notes corrected accordingly. Length 251ft4in and displacement 1,780 tons reconfirmed directly against Wikipedia. Tropical Storm Nate (Oct 2017) cause of tipping reconfirmed.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-checked population figure against Cayman Islands Department of Environment (doe.ky) bi-annual survey reporting, run with Guy Harvey Research Institute — recent counts range ~90-113 individuals, broadly stable around 100; existing '~100' description reconfirmed as accurate and now cited to the official DOE source rather than tourism blogs alone. Species (Hypanus americanus) and depth (4-5m) reconfirmed, no changes.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-checked wall start depth (18ft/~5.5m) and site count (destination360.com lists 22 named sites along Bloody Bay/Jackson Bight, consistent with 'a dozen+' framing) — no factual corrections needed. Nassau grouper habituation and 1-mile wall length reconfirmed.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Silverside season CORRECTED — multiple re-pulled sources (divephotoguide.com, general aggregation of dive blogs) most consistently describe June through August/early August as peak season, with some extending into September; the previous 'August-September only' framing was too narrow. Description widened to 'June-September, most reliable July-August'. Depth 4-15m and Eden Rock adjacency reconfirmed.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-pulled oceanfrontiers.com directly — pinnacle rising from 100ft+ to 45ft top reconfirmed verbatim; black coral, purple sea fans, barrel sponges, chromis, barracuda, stoplight parrotfish, queen angels all reconfirmed as site-specific. No corrections needed. Eagle rays/reef sharks remain correctly excluded as unconfirmed site-specific claims.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Coordinates and West Bay/North Wall location reconfirmed. Pinnacle top ~50ft/15m reconfirmed by independent re-search. Note: a cita.ky 'Dive 365: Ghost Mountain' page surfaced in search results describing a pass-through hole at ~110ft (33m) with a 'do not swim through' warning, but the live cita.ky page now 404s (CITA appears to have removed its Dive 365 site-guide pages entirely) — this detail could NOT be independently confirmed against live content and was deliberately NOT added to the markdown. Sponge/gorgonian marine life description reconfirmed, no changes.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-checked depth against divebooker.com, which describes 'best diving depth' at 30-40m (98-130ft) for advanced divers extending along the wall beyond the 30m recreational exit point already on file — noted in markdown as an option for advanced divers rather than changing the primary max depth field. Northwest Point location, blacktip/Caribbean reef shark sightings, and current-prone conditions all reconfirmed.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Depth WIDENED from 10m to 12m — tortugadivers.com gives 25-40ft (7.6-12.2m), a wider range than the previously recorded flat 10m; JSON depth field updated to 12m (upper bound) and markdown now states the 7.6-12m range explicitly. 1,389 gross tons / 375ft length reconfirmed via web cross-check (caymancompass.com wreck listing could not be re-fetched this pass — blocked by 403 — so it was not added as a source). Three-bladed propellers CONFIRMED as visible surviving structure by 2 independent sources (Red Sail, Tortuga) — the previous 'needs verification' hedge has been removed. One source (NUMA) recounts an unverified single-source anecdote about the captain funding a waterfront church with salvaged cargo proceeds — NOT added to markdown per 2-source historical-fact rule (no corroboration found).

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-searched specifically for 'Chinese Wall' Grand Cayman South Side — still no site-specific source found (only generic South Side wall-diving pages, e.g. activecaribbeantravel.com noting South Side walls start ~70ft). validated remains false per policy — left as unresolved rather than padded with weak sources.

RE-AUDIT 2026-07-23: Re-checked against divessi.com — average depth 16m/52.5ft, max depth 30m/98.4ft reconfirmed matching existing 30m figure. Best season April-October reconfirmed by an independent source and added as a markdown tip. Spotted eagle rays, groupers, moray eels reconfirmed as site-specific; Caribbean reef sharks remain correctly unconfirmed as regular residents.

Site-specific sources not found for Japanese Garden specifically beyond general references to South Side shallow reef. Validated=false — 3 independent site-specific sources not confirmed. Marine life replaced with regional South Side reef description; specific species claims removed.

Named after Dr. James 'Jimmie' Poulson — Grand Cayman's first diving doctor who set up the hyperbaric chamber. Vessel is Japanese cable-laying ship, ~70-80ft long. Sunk 1981 or 1982 (sources differ). First artificial reef in Grand Cayman. Eagle rays, nurse sharks, turtles removed as unconfirmed site-specific residents. Parrotfish and schooling fish confirmed.

CRITICAL CORRECTION: Depth corrected from 50m to 26m (stern at ~85ft). Previous claim of 50m depth was incorrect. Ship is Koni II class (not generic 'Soviet frigate'). Hurricane Ivan (not generic '2004 storm') broke it in two. Named after Captain Keith Parker Tibbetts — Cayman Brac's first National Hero (seafarer, businessman, Legislative Assembly member). Marine life: Nassau grouper and snappers confirmed; former resident Goliath groupers (Boris and Doris) noted as not recently sighted. Eagle rays/turtles qualified as regional.

Three converging coral canyons on West Wall confirmed. Site is NOT true caves — coral canyon swim-throughs with natural light throughout. The Firm (1993) film connection confirmed. Marine life: tarpon, barracuda at exits, spotted lobster, silversides (seasonal), reef fish confirmed. Nurse sharks in canyon bases qualified as occasional.

Also known as Three Fathom Wall. Starts at approximately 18ft (5.5m). Junction of Bloody Bay Wall and Jackson Bight confirmed. Marine life: Caribbean reef sharks, nurse sharks, horse-eye jacks, sea turtles, yellow-headed jawfish, Bermuda chubs, eagle rays, groupers, snappers all confirmed by Little Cayman Divers site-specific accounts.
